quotes.text: In Congress, I’ll push for three commonsense principles: tech companies have to pay their own way, covering the energy and infrastructure costs their data centers create instead of shifting them onto everyday ratepayers; new facilities should be powered by clean, affordable energy, not straining our existing grid or driving up costs; and communities deserve a real seat at the table — full transparency about water and energy usage before a project breaks ground, not after.

I support federal disclosure requirements: any political ad that uses AI-generated or manipulated audio, images, or video should be clearly and prominently labeled as such, the same way we require “paid for by” disclaimers today. Deceptive deepfakes designed to put false words in a candidate’s mouth close to an election should carry legal consequences with a real mechanism for enforcement. Voters deserve to know when they’re looking at reality and when they’re looking at a fabrication.

I hope to see the state give San Diego the authority to decide when and how this technology is deployed in our city. Vehicles deployed in our city should be regulated locally. It’s this way for other vehicles; driverless vehicles cannot be the exception, especially as we learn in real time the rapidly changing nature of AI and AV.
